references.text: The instruction to wash the entrails and legs of the ram, and burn the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord, given to Moses on Mount Sinai.
The description of the burnt offering where the entrails and legs are washed with water, and the priest burns everything on the altar as an offering made by fire with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The washing of the entrails and legs before the burnt offering is burned as an offering made by fire with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The preceding verse describing the presentation of the ram for the burnt offering during the priestly consecration ceremony.
Noah's burnt offering after the flood, where the Lord smelled the pleasing aroma—the first mention of 'pleasing aroma' in Scripture.
Moses' obedience to all that the Lord commanded him, as also emphasized in Leviticus 8:21.
Christ's sacrifice as a fragrant offering to God, fulfilling the typology of the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
